summary: Navina Lamminger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Munich, where she studied under Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Nawang Tsering Shakspo (born 1952) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Lal Mani Joshi and served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).
Neal Donner works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of British Columbia, where his teachers included Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).

Nenghai Shi (1886–1967) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Peking University under Kecheng Zhang, trained under several traditional teachers, founded the Shaocheng Society of Buddhist Studies, and served as vice-president of the Buddhist Association of China (1953–1966).
Ng-Fung Yuen specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Yuen earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngak Sé Rigpé Dorjé studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok and Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro.
Ngakchang Gönpo Tsé Ten studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ngan-che Chan works in Buddhist studies. Chan completed a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin (attested 2007) and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.
Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held positions at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.
Ngawang Lek Shé Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Ngawang Wangyal (1901–1983) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a geshe degree at Drepung Monastery, studied under Agvan Dorzhiev, founded the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center and the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, and taught at Columbia University (~1962–1970).

Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He later taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khenpo Shenga.

Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery and trained under teachers including Yeshe Päldrup, Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at Punjabi University under Inder Mohan Singh (attested 2012) and also studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet (attested 2012).
Nguyen Thi Xinh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She pursued her PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).

Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Hoa completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre (attested 2009).
Nguyen Van Thuong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi, where K. T. S. Sarao served as his MA supervisor.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied at Beijing Institute of Technology and trained under multiple traditional teachers. He worked in Buddhist studies, headed the Central People's Broadcasting Station, and served as a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (~1953–1978).

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Rissho University, Jodo Shu Daigakuin, Shingonshu Rengo Daigaku, Hōryūji Kingakuin, Kogi Shingonshu Rengo Kyoto Gakurin, and Kennin-ji, and founded Nipponzan-Myōhōji.

Nicholas Dirks (born 1950) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Wesleyan University and the University of Chicago, he held academic posts at Caltech (~1978–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).
